correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md establishes the full seven conjugacy-class involution census for ordinary elliptic characteristic-two Artin–Schreier covers of genus q+1 with q=2^h>=8. The central elements are u,t^(q/2),ut^(q/2), and reflections split by parity and u exponent; conjugation t:w_i->w_(i+2) proves four reflection classes. The known two short G-orbits yield fixed counts q,0,2 and the complementary odd-reflection pair 4/0. Because X is ordinary and each involution is weakly ramified, Riemann–Hurwitz with different contribution 2 per fixed point gives g(Y)=(q+2-r)/2. The central nondeck quotients have elliptic degree-two maps and genus >=5, excluding their hyperellipticity by Castelnuovo–Severi; reflection quotients inherit an involution with quotient E/<r>≅P1. For the four-fixed odd reflection, the biquadratic function field gives the reduced Artin–Schreier equation with q/2 simple poles at elliptic-orbit images and coefficients lambda(dx/omega)_P, independent of the representative because in char 2 the inversion-translation preserves omega. The local unramified base change and vanishing of extraneous poles establish the claimed branch passport, not merely an experimental genus formula. Independently reconstructed dihedral multiplication, two short orbit coset actions and involution counts at q=8,16,32, agreeing in all seven classes. The two-orbit structure/weak ramification themselves are cited primary hypotheses, not re-proved in the artifact; this qualification is explicit.

originality.rationale: The classification and short-orbit facts of Tafazolian are prior background. The assessed increment is the simultaneous geometry of all seven involution quotients, distinguishing free central genus q/2+1 nonhyperelliptic from free odd-reflection hyperelliptic, together with a residue-normalized AS equation for the minimal genus quotient. Group-theoretic conjugacy by itself would not provide local ramification coefficients. Relevant G&K primary text on extremal characteristic-two groups was read, and Resultary queried for equivalent quotient/passport statements. No inspected theorem was found to imply the complete claim; this is best-of-knowledge only since Tafazolian and the 2015 J. Algebra full text were not accessible at the requested depth. A priority uncertainty of that magnitude remains documented rather than replaced by a fictitious negative finding.

value.rationale: The problem naturally asks how the many involutions of a well-structured maximal automorphism group act on an explicit ordinary high-genus cover. Simultaneously determining fixed sets, quotient genus, ordinary/hyperelliptic distinctions and branch coefficients makes the full geometric quotient passport calculable. Genus alone does not identify isomorphism class, and the coefficient formula offers concrete data for comparing quotients, beyond classifying the abstract automorphism group. The claim is restricted to the residue-uniform ordinary elliptic cover over algebraically closed characteristic two and q>=8; it does not claim arbitrary base-field descent.
